title: Hosted API - embeddings + rerank demo (MapleSearch)
summary: Intro + demo of Redwood hosted embeddings and reranking endpoints for improving search relevance. Discussed integration patterns, latency vs cost tradeoffs, security (VPC/SSO/KMS), and rollout strategy. Agreed next steps: send pricing, SSO and SOC2 docs, and run a scoped benchmark with 10k queries.

transcript_header:
Date: 2027-11-01
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Ruth Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (MapleSearch - Head of Search), Devon Park (MapleSearch - Backend Eng), Aisha Khan (MapleSearch - PM)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call? um I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Samir and Ruth are our SEs.
[00:09] Lena Ortiz: Lena here. Hi.
[00:11] Devon Park: Devon, hi.
[00:13] Aisha Khan: Aisha, hi all.
[00:15] Maya Chen: Awesome. We'll do a quick agenda — 10 minute discovery, then demo of embeddings + reranking, followed by Q&A and next steps. Sound good?
[00:26] Lena Ortiz: Yup, perfect. We're mainly looking at improving our search relevance across web and help center, reduce chaff and also keep latency under 120ms p50 ideally.
[00:36] Samir Patel: Got it. Can you remind us of the current stack and traffic profile?
[00:40] Lena Ortiz: Sure — we use Elastic Search for indexing, results are paged through our service layer — about 1.5M queries/day, peak QPS around 120. We have a relevance model but it's pretty static; we want to add semantic reranking and embeddings for semantic match, especially for long tail queries.
[00:56] Devon Park: We also have strict PII policy — anything that touches user data needs to be encrypted and auditable.
[01:03] Ruth Alvarez: Totally — Redwood hosted supports encryption at rest and in transit, and we can integrate with customer KMS for private key control.
[01:10] Aisha Khan: Timeline wise, we'd like a POC in 3 weeks if possible.
[01:14] Maya Chen: Good to know. We'll show a hosted path that should be quick to integrate and a plan for a POC.
[01:21] Samir Patel: OK diving into the demo. I'll share my screen — starting with the embeddings endpoint. So, Redwood's hosted embeddings API returns dense vectors, we have multiple models tuned for retrieval, and the SDKs are straightforward. Example call: POST /v1/embeddings with text payload, get back 768/1024-d floats.
[01:40] Devon Park: Are those models quantized? We care about memory footprint if someone self-hosts later.
[01:45] Samir Patel: Hosted models are optimized; we provide quantized variants for Dedicated/private, but hosted is managed. For your POC we can use the 1536-d model for better recall.
[01:56] [01:58] Maya Chen: Aisha, earlier you mentioned cost targets?
[02:02] Aisha Khan: We're targeting under $10k/month for inference depending on scope — for the initial POC it's more flexible.
[02:09] Samir Patel: Good to keep in mind. Next I’ll demo a simple search flow: embed query -> ANN nearest neighbor lookup -> take top N candidates -> call our rerank endpoint which takes the original query, doc text and doc embedding to produce a score and optionally a compact explanation.
[02:28] Samir Patel: Sharing a sample rerank payload now.
[02:31] [02:33] Devon Park: What's the latency profile for the rerank step? If we send top 10 candidates, what's p50 and p95?
[02:38] Samir Patel: For hosted rerank with our mid-tier model, p50 is ~25-35ms per item when batched intelligently, p95 around 120-180ms depending on sequence length. If you rerank 10 docs in a single call, we typically see aggregate p50 under 80ms. These are approximate; we'll run your benchmark.
[02:56] Lena Ortiz: Hmm p95 of 180ms might be high for us; our SLO is 120ms p95.
[03:03] Samir Patel: Totally — there are levers: smaller rerank model, token truncation, batching levels, or using a hybrid approach where embeddings filter more aggressively and rerank only 5 items. Also consider caching repeated queries.
[03:16] Aisha Khan: Can cached results be invalidated on content update?
[03:20] Ruth Alvarez: Yes; we surface TTLs and eviction controls and you can attach cache key versioning on your side.
[03:26] [03:28] Devon Park: Security question — does Redwood host customer data? We need to ensure data residency and logs for audit.
[03:33] Maya Chen: For hosted we store embeddings ephemeral by default unless you enable persistent storage; we have SOC2 and can enable retention settings, plus audit logs. For full control we have Dedicated or Private deploys.
[03:48] Lena Ortiz: We may start hosted as an eval but Dedicated may be required if contract goes enterprise.
[03:53] Samir Patel: Makes sense. Now walking through the console — you can view token/cost breakdowns by route, per-model dashboards, and rerank latency histograms. I'll flip to the 'Optimize' tab to show batching suggestions and quantization notes based on workload.
[04:10] [04:12] Samir Patel: Here's a sample chroma/ANN integration — client embeds stored in your vector DB, queries embed -> ANN search returns top k -> we call /v1/rerank with an array of candidates. The rerank API returns scores and optional structured output you can use to surface reasons.
[04:28] Aisha Khan: Is there example code for the ANN layer? We use Faiss currently.
[04:33] Samir Patel: Yep, we've got Faiss examples in the docs and a benchmark workbook for Faiss + Redwood embeddings. I'll share that.
[04:40] [04:42] Devon Park: What about throughput — if we hit 120 QPS and need to rerank top 5 for each, do you support rate limits and burst policies?
[04:49] Ruth Alvarez: Yes, hosted tiers have rate limiting; for scale we recommend a Dedicated pool with predictable throughput or configuring burst capacity. We can model your cost given your QPS and expected tokens per call.
[05:01] Lena Ortiz: Can we do a canary rollout? We want to A/B test relevance before full swap.
[05:06] Maya Chen: Absolutely — Console supports canary routes and rollbacks with traffic splits. You can route a subset to the new reranker and compare metrics.
[05:14] [05:16] Samir Patel: Demoing the rerank request/response — sending a batch of 6 candidates now... response includes scores and a short rationale field. Note: sometimes the auto-gen rationale can be noisy, we recommend using it as signal not single-source truth.
[05:31] Devon Park: The rationale output might leak PII if it includes user content — can we sanitize?
[05:36] Ruth Alvarez: You can disable text-level rationale and only use scalar scores; also we support redaction hooks in the pipeline.
[05:43] Aisha Khan: How long would a POC take? We asked for 3 weeks earlier.
[05:47] Maya Chen: For a scoped POC — ingest sample corpus, run embeddings + ANN baseline, then run rerank evaluation — 2-4 weeks is typical. We'll provide a plan.
[05:57] [06:00] Lena Ortiz: What's the pricing model for embeddings+rerank? Per token for rerank and per embedding vector for embeddings?
[06:06] Maya Chen: Correct — embeddings billed per request vector unit, rerank billed per token processed, and there's a small hosting / per-route fee for logging/observability. We'll send a detailed price sheet.
[06:18] Devon Park: Any examples of customers who replaced Elastic rerank with this flow?
[06:23] Samir Patel: We have a few references in retail and help center workloads; I'll redact names in the doc we share but can provide reference calls if you want.
[06:31] [06:35] Aisha Khan: Can we run a benchmark against our baseline model and get an ROC/AUC or MRR comparison?
[06:39] Samir Patel: Yes — our benchmark template includes MRR, NDCG, top-k precision. We'll run with your labels and return aggregated stats.
[06:47] Lena Ortiz: Network wise, we need to ensure our firewall can call Redwood endpoints — no inbound connections needed, right?
[06:52] Ruth Alvarez: Correct, outbound only. We can provide IP ranges and NAT details for allowlisting.
[06:59] [07:02] Devon Park: For sampling: we have 10k queries and click labels — is that enough?
[07:07] Samir Patel: Good starting point; more is better but 10k with labels will give meaningful signals. We'll try to keep the POC scoped to 10k.
[07:14] Maya Chen: Quick pause does anyone have burning security questions?
[07:19] Lena Ortiz: SOC2 report and SAML SSO are musts for procurement.
[07:23] Maya Chen: We'll include SOC2 and SAML docs in the pack.
[07:27] [07:30] Samir Patel: Now a quick live example — searching "refund policy for late shipments" — embedding query, ANN returns 20 candidates, we rerank top 8. See how semantic matches bubble up even if keywords are different.
[07:46] Aisha Khan: Nice — that example actually surfaces the support article we wanted.
[07:50] Devon Park: I noticed some word substitution in the transcript, ah I mean in the rerank rationale it says 'shipment' spelled weirdly sometimes — is that a tokenizer issue?
[07:58] Samir Patel: Could be tokenization or OCR on historical docs; we can pre-process and normalize.
[08:03] [08:06] Lena Ortiz: Any compliance about data deletion? If we send queries, can Redwood guarantee deletion after POC?
[08:11] Maya Chen: Yes — hosted endpoints have retention settings and we can run a purge request; for enterprise you can opt for no-persistence. We'll add that to the security pack.
[08:23] Samir Patel: I'm going to show the Console's rerank comparison widget — it shows before/after results and MRR/NDCG deltas per query set. You can upload labeled queries and get an automated evaluation.
[08:36] Aisha Khan: That's helpful for product.
[08:39] [08:43] Devon Park: Any pitfalls we should watch for during integration?
[08:47] Ruth Alvarez: Watch token lengths for rerank inputs — long documents inflate latency and cost. Truncate or pass excerpts. Also pay attention to batching — inefficient batching raises latency. We'll provide best-practices doc.
[09:00] Maya Chen: Ok wrapping up — we'll send the pricing/security pack, Samir will share rerank payload examples and a benchmark template, you'll provide 10k queries. Schedule POC kickoff for week of 11/15.
[09:13] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good.
[09:15] Devon Park: Thanks everyone.
[09:17] Aisha Khan: Appreciate it.
[09:19] Maya Chen: Thanks all — talk soon.
[09:22] [End of recording]
questions: What is p50/p95 latency for rerank with top N candidates?
Can we use customer KMS for keys?
How to set up canary rollouts and measure MRR/NDCG?
